_comment: PROTOTYPE — HELD-OUT adversarial set. Invented prose, not W34 data, deliberately parked on the boundary of #6's two rule sentences. Its job is to find the margin: W34 is 8 rows the screener passes 3/3, which proves it works on the only batch we have and says nothing about how close the edge is. LABELS HERE ARE A JUDGEMENT CALL, not #6's — where the model disagrees, read it first as evidence that the rule sentence is underspecified, and only then as a model failure.

rows.notes: Their old agency contacted us last year about a similar project.
rows.why: N1 is about THIS contact having been reached before. An agency is somebody else. Silent.

rows.notes: We ran a campaign into this segment in the spring; nobody from this account replied.
rows.why: Names an earlier campaign and then rules the match out. N2 needs a MATCH with an earlier campaign, not the mere existence of one. The strongest negative in the set.

rows.notes: Rohan updated his email signature to the new domain after the rebrand.
rows.why: A different email address with no earlier contact behind it. N1's clause is 'an earlier contact under a different email address' — the earlier contact is the load-bearing half.

rows.notes: Duplicate of the row above — same company, same person, submitted twice by the form.
rows.why: A duplicate the pipeline proves from the data. ADR-0002's exclusion. This is the row that should separate prompt v1 from v2 if the exclusions are load-bearing at all.

rows.notes: Sat next to our CEO at a conference in March and asked for a follow-up.
rows.why: An earlier contact with this very person, but nothing about a different email address and no campaign. Both rules turn on a clause this note does not contain. The hardest negative: a screener reaching for 'have we seen them before?' rather than the written rule will fire here.

rows.notes: Mail bounced from her old work address, so this is the current one.
rows.why: N1 with none of #6's vocabulary. Tests whether the rule generalises past the wording Heliograph happens to use.

rows.notes: Appears in the Q1 outbound list under a slightly different company name.
rows.why: N2 with none of #6's vocabulary, and the match is on the company rather than the person.

rows.notes: We emailed him at a previous address during the winter push and he never replied.
rows.why: Both kinds from ONE sentence, where Lattice Forge gets one sentence each. Tests whether two kinds can share a single span of evidence — the co-occurrence question at its most awkward.
